title: JavaScript Event Loop Core Check
description: Check your understanding of the JavaScript engine, runtime, call stack, microtasks, macrotasks, rendering, and concurrency model.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does the JavaScript engine do?

options.text: Provides the DOM API by itself
Turns every callback into a class

questions.explanation: The engine parses and executes JavaScript. Runtime environments provide APIs like DOM, timers, and fetch.

questions.prompt: Which is usually provided by the runtime rather than the core JavaScript language?
questions.explanation: Timers like `setTimeout` are provided by the browser or Node runtime.

questions.prompt: What does the call stack track?

options.text: All files in a module folder

questions.explanation: The call stack tracks active function calls and unwinds as they finish.

questions.prompt: What error can runaway recursion cause?
questions.explanation: Recursion without a stopping condition can overflow the call stack.

questions.prompt: Which callback type is commonly a microtask?
questions.explanation: Promise callbacks such as `.then`, `.catch`, and `.finally` are microtasks.

questions.prompt: Which callback type is commonly a macrotask?
In the simplified event-loop model, what runs first after synchronous code finishes?
questions.explanation: After the call stack clears, queued microtasks run before the next macrotask.

options.text: Schedule `fn` to run later when the event loop can pick it
Run `fn` immediately before the next line

questions.explanation: `setTimeout(..., 0)` schedules a future task. It does not interrupt current synchronous code.

questions.prompt: What can long synchronous work do in the browser?

options.text: Block rendering, timers, and user input handling
Force microtasks to run before synchronous code
Automatically move work to a Web Worker

questions.explanation: Long tasks keep the main thread busy, delaying rendering and callbacks.

options.text: Always running JavaScript code on many threads at once

questions.explanation: Concurrency means making progress on multiple tasks over time; it is not the same as parallel JavaScript execution.

options.text: Scheduling animation-related work before a repaint

questions.explanation: `requestAnimationFrame` helps align visual updates with the browser rendering cycle.

questions.prompt: What is the simplest prediction model for many event-loop examples?

options.text: Timers, then synchronous code, then promises

questions.explanation: For many beginner examples, run synchronous stack code first, then microtasks, then task/macrotask callbacks.
